answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can earn fees, and a randomly selected counterparty can challenge its work. A proven duplicate identity loses the stake, while honest agents recover theirs after a delay. Splitting one operator across many accounts therefore multiplies capital tied up and risks forfeiture without multiplying the real work or trust earned. A lantern audit may use yarrow as a challenge seed and nectar as the fee at risk.
